scope: Tauri Rust 2.12.0, tauri-build 2.7.0 and keyring 4.2.0 with pinned Rust 1.90.0
tests: device-identity.test.ts: backend errors, partial identity, interrupted writes, concurrent initialization and legitimate signing
native cross-process identity lock and immutable identity-write tests on Linux, Windows and macOS
multi-platform Tauri cargo test and build jobs
repository required CI, Security, Tri-App, Main Verification, and Release Policy checks
risk_notes: Global Node ambient types can hide browser/WebView runtime errors.
TypeScript 6 changes compiler behavior and may expose stricter library declarations.
Desktop frontend and Node test environments must remain independently type-checked.
Credential-store upgrades must preserve ai.omnidesk.desktop service identifiers, existing device identities, native backends, and fail-closed error propagation.
Incomplete native identity records now require explicit secure-store recovery instead of silently rotating surviving credentials.
Native identity writes use an OS file lock in application-local data and reject replacement; operator-token updates retain their prior behavior.

Tauri 2.12 requires Rust 1.90: all build, security and release workflow pins must advance together. Rust 1.90 changes the Linux default linker to LLD; locked native tests on Linux, macOS and Windows and isolated optimized glib regressions remain required.
rollback_steps: Restore package.json, package-lock.json, and TypeScript configs from the parent main commit.
Restore Cargo.lock and all synchronized Rust toolchain pins from the approved parent if native regression is observed; do not export or migrate secrets to plaintext.
Run npm ci, npm run typecheck, npm test, npm run build, and Tauri multi-platform checks before redeployment.
validation_boundary: GitHub required checks on the pull-request head are authoritative and fail closed.
